the difference in conformation between fusogenically active and nonactive F proteins of SV5 on the cell surface and with the mechanism of the activation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L22P mutation induces a subtle conformational change in the WR F1 and F0 proteins that is required for the fusion activity of the F protein in the absence of the HN protein.

the amino acid at position 22 of F2 is a determinant for fusogenic activity of the SV5 F protein and that the amino acid sequence in the middle of the F1 subunit is a determinant for the difference in conformation between fusogenically active L22P and nonfusogenically active WR F protein on the cell surface.
the L22P mutation in the WR F gene is not only necessary but also sufficient to confer the fusogenic activity on the SV5 F protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusogenicity of SV5 F protein is determined by the difference in native conformations between fusogenic and nonfusogenic F proteins on the cell surface.
L22P is a mutant F protein that has lost its dependence on HN protein for fusion activity and that the amino acid residue Leu-22 is a critical determinant for this loss of HN dependence.
L22P, which is a mutant of the nonfusogenic SV5 F protein, can be used as a model for the fusogenic paramyxovirus fusion (F) proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a paramyxovirus fusion protein can be activated to a fusogenic state without HN protein.
a single amino acid substitution in the SV5 F protein can alter its conformation in a manner that allows it to be fusogenic in the absence of the HN protein.
the F protein of a nonfusogenic SV5 strain (WR) can be converted into a fusogenic form by a single amino acid replacement in subunit F2.
